name: Receive purchased materials
scope: Catalogue scenario only; not an installed customer capability
outcome: Know what arrived, what remains on order, and what stock is available for work
questions: Where do you keep stock: warehouse, vans, or both?
Do suppliers deliver orders in parts?
Do you reserve stock for jobs before it is used?
Who may receive deliveries and correct mistakes?
rules: Receive a positive whole quantity no greater than the outstanding order quantity
Keep the order open until all ordered units are received
Increase on-hand stock without changing job reservations
Retain a delivery reference for each receipt
Never approve or pay a bill as a side effect of receiving
acceptance: Receive 8 of 24 units: 16 remain outstanding; availability rises by 8
Receive the remaining 16: the order is complete and further receipt is unavailable
Reject zero, negative, fractional and excessive quantities without changing stock
Retain entered values and delivery reference after a validation failure
Reject a stale receipt revision without applying it twice
provenance: Bedrock Workbench design exploration, September 2026; synthetic examples

nodes.name: Number
nodes.description: A numeric value. Its business meaning comes from the quantity or field that contains it.
rules: Use decimal arithmetic for measured quantities; do not silently round.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Text
nodes.description: Human-readable words such as a part name or delivery reference.
rules: Validation belongs to the field context.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Identifier
nodes.description: A stable reference to a record, independent of its display name.
rules: Controls select by identifier, never by a label that could change.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Image reference
nodes.description: Optional supporting media owned by the business.
rules: A missing image is valid; image descriptions must be supplied where meaningful.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Stocking unit
nodes.description: How a quantity is counted or measured.

fields.name: precision
fields.meaning: Allowed fractional digits for this item

rules: Each and box use whole counts in this demo; measured stock may permit fractions.
Conversions between purchase and stocking units are not implemented.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Quantity
nodes.description: A value paired with its unit; “8” alone does not say 8 of what.
rules: Compare or add quantities only in compatible units.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Inventory item
nodes.description: The identity and description of a stocked part, independent of where it is kept.
rules: An item can have many stock positions, one per location.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Stock location
nodes.description: A place holding stock, such as a warehouse or van.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Stock position
nodes.description: Quantities for one item at one location. Availability is a derived value, not another editable count.
rules: The demo does not permit negative stock or reservations exceeding on hand.
A real business must explicitly decide how backorders and negative availability work.
Stock changes through business actions, not by editing the displayed availability.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Purchase order line
nodes.description: The ordered item and quantities used to validate a delivery.
rules: The demonstrated order contains one line of 24 whole units.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Receipt
nodes.description: A recorded delivery with a reference and quantity; changes stock through a controlled action.

fields.name: zone
fields.meaning: Zone used to enter the arrival time

rules: Quantity is positive, whole and no greater than outstanding for this example.
Receiving adds to on hand without changing reservations.
Receiving neither approves nor pays a supplier bill.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Calendar date
nodes.description: A day on the calendar, without a time or time zone.
rules: Never convert a date-only value through UTC; that can change its day.
Use for due dates, promised delivery days and all-day planning.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Local time
nodes.description: A time of day without a date or zone; it is not an exact moment.
rules: Pair with a date and IANA time zone before resolving an instant.
Useful for opening hours; recurring schedules are not implemented in this example.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Time zone
nodes.description: An IANA region whose rules determine local time and daylight-saving changes.
rules: An abbreviation or fixed offset is not a substitute for a scheduling zone.
Time-zone rule updates travel through maintained application dependencies.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Timestamp
nodes.description: An exact instant, stored in UTC and displayed with explicit local-zone context.
rules: Do not treat a datetime-local input as an instant without a zone.
Reject nonexistent local times and ambiguous repeated times instead of silently choosing.
The example rejects repeated times; an explicit earlier/later occurrence chooser is future work.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Elapsed duration
nodes.description: An elapsed amount of time, expressed with an explicit unit.
rules: Elapsed duration can differ from wall-clock difference across daylight-saving changes.
A calendar day is not always 24 elapsed hours.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Date range
nodes.description: Two calendar dates defining an inclusive span.
rules: End must be on or after start; a single-day range is valid.
A timestamp filter applies these dates in its stated reporting time zone.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Scheduled window
nodes.description: A start and end instant plus the scheduling zone.
rules: End must be strictly after start; overnight work uses the next calendar date.
Intervals are half-open: a booking ending at 11:00 may meet one starting at 11:00.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Appointment
nodes.description: A scheduled work window for a resource, such as a crew.
rules: This demonstration rejects overlapping bookings for Crew A.
Recurring bookings, resource permissions, cancellation and cross-user concurrency are not implemented.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

nodes.name: Stock movement
nodes.description: A receipt or transfer event, with occurrence time distinct from record-entry time.
rules: Keep occurrence and recording times distinct when entering events later.
Stock quantities change through validated actions; changing a displayed date never rewrites stock.
Transfer entries are read-only fixtures here; transfer commands and persistent ledgers are not implemented.
nodes.scope: Conceptual business type; sample values are synthetic.

presentation_bindings.name: Choose an inventory item
presentation_bindings.purpose: Identify the correct part while seeing its location-specific availability.
presentation_bindings.rule: Selecting a part changes view state only. Availability is contextual information, not a reservation or promise of stock.
presentation_bindings.empty: Show no matching items and allow filters to be cleared.
presentation_bindings.scope: One synthetic stock position per item; location is visible in each option. Real deployments require an explicit location and freshness policy.

presentation_bindings.name: Inspect stock
presentation_bindings.purpose: Compare quantities and inspect the selected part.
presentation_bindings.rule: Derived availability is read-only; receiving is a separate business action.

presentation_bindings.name: Record a delivery
presentation_bindings.purpose: Capture a received quantity and reference, then apply the receiving rules.
presentation_bindings.rule: Validate before recording; increment received and on-hand quantities while preserving reservations. The demo uses session-local state, not persistent transactions.

presentation_bindings.name: Schedule warehouse work
presentation_bindings.purpose: Book a crew with explicit local-zone intent and an exact elapsed duration.
presentation_bindings.rule: Validate both zoned instants, positive interval and no overlap with the same crew. Adjacent bookings are allowed.

presentation_bindings.name: Record when stock arrived
presentation_bindings.purpose: Distinguish the physical arrival from the later entry of that event.
presentation_bindings.rule: Resolve the entered local time with its zone. Generate recorded_at at command time, never from an editable field.

presentation_bindings.name: Review stock movements by date
presentation_bindings.purpose: Review receipts and transfers occurring within a calendar date range.
presentation_bindings.rule: Both dates are included in America/Toronto. Invalid ranges retain the last valid result set. Filtering never changes stock.

presentation_bindings.name: Check packaging
presentation_bindings.purpose: Complete or reopen the synthetic packaging check.
presentation_bindings.rule: Toggles the session check only; no attachments or durable evidence are captured.

Assign recording time when the command succeeds.

failures: Invalid local time, reversed interval or overlap retains input.
